algorithms.assumptions: Canonical event-horizon semantics require finite strictly positive objective values and minimization. Maximization or non-positive costs are rejected rather than silently transformed.
algorithms.convergence: No universal finite-time global convergence guarantee is asserted; random event-horizon replacement maintains exploration while attraction concentrates stars around the current black hole.

algorithms.name: Symbiotic Organisms Search
algorithms.time: O(ND) per cycle plus 4N objective evaluations
algorithms.applicability: Bounded continuous derivative-free optimization with parameter-free mutualism, commensalism and parasitism phases
algorithms.publication: Cheng and Prayogo (2014), Symbiotic Organisms Search: A new metaheuristic optimization algorithm, Computers & Structures 139, 98-112
algorithms.implementation: Canonical SOS with mutualism benefit factors in {1,2}, commensalism random factor in [-1,1], parasite-vector mutation, and greedy replacement after each published interaction.
algorithms.assumptions: Finite bounded continuous box, finite objective values and at least two organisms. SOS exposes no algorithm-specific tuning coefficient beyond generic population size and iteration budget.
algorithms.convergence: No universal finite-time global convergence guarantee is asserted; the three canonical symbiosis phases combine directed exploitation and stochastic replacement without algorithm-specific coefficients.

algorithms.name: Multi-Verse Optimizer
algorithms.time: O(ND + N log N) per iteration plus N objective evaluations
algorithms.applicability: Non-negative-cost bounded continuous minimization using white-hole exchange and best-universe wormholes
algorithms.publication: Mirjalili, Mirjalili and Hatamlou (2016), Multi-Verse Optimizer: a nature-inspired algorithm for global optimization, Neural Computing and Applications 27, 495-513
algorithms.implementation: Canonical minimization-oriented MVO white-hole roulette, normalized inflation rates, elite best universe, linearly increasing wormhole existence probability and power-law travelling distance rate with p=6 by default.
algorithms.assumptions: Finite bounded continuous box and finite non-negative inflation rates. The original minimization-oriented normalized-inflation/roulette semantics are preserved; maximization and negative objective values are rejected rather than silently transformed.
algorithms.convergence: No universal finite-time global convergence guarantee is asserted; WEP increases exploitation while TDR decreases the maximum wormhole displacement according to the published p-controlled schedule.

algorithms.name: Equilibrium Optimizer
algorithms.time: O(ND) per iteration plus N objective evaluations
algorithms.applicability: Bounded continuous derivative-free optimization using an equilibrium pool, exponential turnover and generation-rate control
algorithms.publication: Faramarzi, Heidarinejad, Stephens and Mirjalili (2020), Equilibrium optimizer: A novel optimization algorithm, Knowledge-Based Systems 191, 105190
algorithms.implementation: Canonical EO with four best equilibrium candidates plus their average, a1=2, a2=1, GP=0.5 defaults, exponential F term, generation probability and source-code memory saving.
algorithms.assumptions: Finite bounded continuous box, finite objective values and at least four particles. The equilibrium pool contains the four best-so-far candidates and their arithmetic mean; V=1 is the canonical internal constant.
algorithms.convergence: No universal finite-time global convergence guarantee is asserted; the exponential turnover term and generation probability balance exploration and exploitation around the equilibrium pool.

algorithms.name: Inertia Weight Particle Swarm Optimization
algorithms.time: O(ND) movement plus N objective evaluations per iteration
algorithms.applicability: Bounded continuous derivative-free optimization using the 1998 constant inertia-weight PSO mechanism
algorithms.publication: Shi & Eberhart (1998), A Modified Particle Swarm Optimizer, Proceedings of the 1998 IEEE International Conference on Evolutionary Computation, 69-73
algorithms.implementation: Canonical synchronous global-best PSO with explicit constant inertia weight w; it does not silently substitute the later linearly decreasing inertia schedule.
algorithms.assumptions: Finite bounded continuous box, finite objective values, synchronous personal/global best updates and a constant inertia weight.
algorithms.convergence: No universal global convergence guarantee is asserted; the release preserves the inertia-weight mechanism introduced by Shi and Eberhart without mixing later schedules.

algorithms.name: Clerc-Kennedy Constriction Particle Swarm
algorithms.time: O(ND) movement plus N objective evaluations per iteration
algorithms.applicability: Bounded continuous optimization using the Clerc-Kennedy constriction analysis with phi > 4
algorithms.publication: Clerc & Kennedy (2002), The particle swarm - explosion, stability, and convergence in a multidimensional complex space, IEEE Transactions on Evolutionary Computation 6(1), 58-73
algorithms.implementation: Canonical constriction-factor velocity dynamics with chi computed from phi=c1+c2 and kappa; default c1=c2=2.05, phi=4.10, kappa=1.
algorithms.assumptions: Finite bounded continuous box; phi greater than four for the published constriction expression.
algorithms.convergence: The release implements the published constriction dynamics and exposes the stability-related phi/kappa controls; it does not claim objective-independent global convergence.

algorithms.name: Bare Bones Particle Swarm
algorithms.time: O(ND) Gaussian sampling plus N objective evaluations per iteration
algorithms.applicability: Bounded continuous optimization using velocity-free Gaussian sampling around personal/global best positions
algorithms.publication: Kennedy (2003), Bare bones particle swarms, Proceedings of the 2003 IEEE Swarm Intelligence Symposium, 80-87
algorithms.implementation: Velocity is eliminated. Each coordinate is sampled from a Gaussian centered at (p_i+g)/2 with standard deviation |p_i-g|, followed by bounded repair and personal-best update.
algorithms.assumptions: Finite bounded continuous box and finite objective values; global-best bare-bones form.
algorithms.convergence: No universal finite-time global convergence guarantee is asserted; the release is the velocity-free Gaussian mechanism of Kennedy (2003).

algorithms.name: Fully Informed Particle Swarm
algorithms.time: O(N^2D) for the fully connected unweighted informer structure plus N evaluations per iteration
algorithms.applicability: Bounded continuous optimization where every particle is influenced by all informers rather than a single neighborhood best
algorithms.publication: Mendes, Kennedy & Neves (2004), The Fully Informed Particle Swarm: Simpler, Maybe Better, IEEE Transactions on Evolutionary Computation 8(3), 204-210
algorithms.implementation: Unweighted fully informed structure: total acceleration is divided equally among all informers, with independent random multipliers per informer and coordinate, combined with Clerc-Kennedy constriction.
algorithms.assumptions: Finite bounded continuous box; nonempty informer set; this public identity uses the unweighted fully connected informer structure.
algorithms.convergence: The constriction controls the linearized motion; no universal objective-independent global convergence guarantee is asserted.

algorithms.name: Comprehensive Learning Particle Swarm Optimizer
algorithms.time: O(ND) exemplar-guided movement plus N objective evaluations per iteration
algorithms.applicability: Multimodal bounded continuous global optimization using dimension-wise exemplars learned from different particles
algorithms.publication: Liang, Qin, Suganthan & Baskar (2006), Comprehensive learning particle swarm optimizer for global optimization of multimodal functions, IEEE Transactions on Evolutionary Computation 10(3), 281-295
algorithms.implementation: Dimension-wise comprehensive learning with particle-specific Pc, two-particle tournaments, c=1.49445, inertia 0.9 to 0.4 and refreshing gap m=7.
algorithms.assumptions: Finite bounded continuous domain; particle-specific dimension exemplars and refresh after the configured stagnation gap.
algorithms.convergence: No universal finite-time global convergence guarantee is asserted; the release preserves the published comprehensive-learning mechanism and schedules.

algorithms.name: Cooperative Particle Swarm Optimization (CPSO-SK)
algorithms.time: O(KSD) movement with K*S context-vector objective evaluations per iteration
algorithms.applicability: Bounded continuous optimization benefiting from cooperative decomposition of the decision vector into component subspaces
algorithms.publication: van den Bergh & Engelbrecht (2004), A Cooperative Approach to Particle Swarm Optimization, IEEE Transactions on Evolutionary Computation 8(3), 225-239
algorithms.implementation: CPSO-SK cooperative decomposition: K sub-swarms optimize disjoint components and are evaluated through a shared context vector assembled from the current best component of every sub-swarm.
algorithms.assumptions: Finite bounded continuous vector, deterministic balanced component partition and finite objective values.
algorithms.convergence: No universal global convergence guarantee is asserted; the release is explicitly CPSO-SK and does not silently claim the hybrid CPSO-HK variant.

algorithms.name: Standard Particle Swarm Optimization 2007
algorithms.time: O(ND + N^2) per iteration for explicit adaptive-random informer discovery plus N objective evaluations
algorithms.applicability: Bounded continuous baseline PSO with standardized parameter values and adaptive random local communication
algorithms.publication: Bratton & Kennedy (2007), Defining a Standard for Particle Swarm Optimization, Proceedings of the 2007 IEEE Swarm Intelligence Symposium, 120-127
algorithms.implementation: SPSO-2007 parameterization w=1/(2 ln 2), c=1/2+ln 2, default swarm size 10+floor(2 sqrt(D)), K=3 random informing attempts and topology regeneration on non-improvement.
algorithms.assumptions: Finite bounded continuous box and a nonempty random informer neighborhood for every particle.
algorithms.convergence: The release is a reproducible SPSO-2007 baseline; no objective-independent finite-time global convergence guarantee is asserted.

algorithms.name: Species-Based Particle Swarm Optimization
algorithms.time: O(N^2D) species reconstruction plus O(ND) movement and N objective evaluations per iteration
algorithms.applicability: Static multimodal bounded continuous optimization where multiple species should form around different dominating personal-best seeds
algorithms.publication: Parrott & Li (2006), Locating and tracking multiple dynamic optima by a particle swarm model using speciation, IEEE Transactions on Evolutionary Computation 10(4), 440-458
algorithms.implementation: Static SPSO mode: personal bests are sorted by dominance, species seeds are formed with a distance radius, and each particle uses its current species seed as neighborhood best.
algorithms.problem: \min_{x\in\mathcal X\subseteq\mathbb R^D} f(x)\quad\text{with multiple attraction basins}
algorithms.assumptions: Finite bounded continuous domain, finite objective values and a positive species radius; this release implements the static multimodal SPSO mode, not the dynamic-environment extension.
algorithms.convergence: The method intentionally maintains multiple species and therefore does not assert single-point swarm convergence or a universal global-optimum guarantee.

algorithms.name: NSGA-II
algorithms.time: O(MN^2) nondominated sorting plus objective evaluations per generation
algorithms.applicability: Bounded continuous native multiobjective Pareto optimization
algorithms.publication: Deb, Pratap, Agarwal & Meyarivan (2002), A Fast and Elitist Multiobjective Genetic Algorithm: NSGA-II, IEEE Transactions on Evolutionary Computation 6(2), 182-197
algorithms.implementation: Fast nondominated sorting, elitist parent-offspring survival and crowding-distance diversity.
algorithms.assumptions: Finite bounded continuous decision box, at least two finite objectives, and one explicit OptimizationSense per objective.
algorithms.convergence: No universal finite-time convergence guarantee is asserted; the implementation preserves the named multiobjective mechanism.

algorithms.name: Pareto Archived Evolution Strategy
algorithms.time: O(AM) archive dominance per mutation step
algorithms.applicability: Bounded continuous native multiobjective Pareto optimization
algorithms.publication: Knowles & Corne (2000), Approximating the Nondominated Front Using the Pareto Archived Evolution Strategy, Evolutionary Computation 8(2), 149-172
algorithms.implementation: Canonical (1+1)-PAES local mutation with Pareto archive and adaptive objective-space grid.
algorithms.assumptions: Finite bounded continuous decision box, at least two finite objectives, and one explicit OptimizationSense per objective.
algorithms.convergence: No universal finite-time convergence guarantee is asserted; the implementation preserves the named multiobjective mechanism.

algorithms.name: PESA-II
algorithms.time: O(ANM) archive/grid selection plus objective evaluations
algorithms.applicability: Bounded continuous native multiobjective Pareto optimization
algorithms.publication: Corne, Jerram, Knowles & Oates (2001), PESA-II: Region-Based Selection in Evolutionary Multiobjective Optimization, GECCO 2001, 283-290
algorithms.implementation: Region-based selection from an external nondominated archive using adaptive hyperbox density.
algorithms.assumptions: Finite bounded continuous decision box, at least two finite objectives, and one explicit OptimizationSense per objective.
algorithms.convergence: No universal finite-time convergence guarantee is asserted; the implementation preserves the named multiobjective mechanism.

algorithms.name: Indicator-Based Evolutionary Algorithm
algorithms.time: O(MN^2) binary-indicator fitness per environmental selection
algorithms.applicability: Bounded continuous native multiobjective Pareto optimization
algorithms.publication: Zitzler & Kunzli (2004), Indicator-Based Selection in Multiobjective Search, PPSN VIII, LNCS 3242, 832-842
algorithms.implementation: Binary additive-epsilon indicator fitness directly drives environmental selection.
algorithms.assumptions: Finite bounded continuous decision box, at least two finite objectives, and one explicit OptimizationSense per objective.
algorithms.convergence: No universal finite-time convergence guarantee is asserted; the implementation preserves the named multiobjective mechanism.

algorithms.name: MOEA/D
algorithms.time: O(NTM) neighborhood scalarization updates plus objective evaluations
algorithms.applicability: Bounded continuous native multiobjective Pareto optimization
algorithms.publication: Zhang & Li (2007), MOEA/D: A Multiobjective Evolutionary Algorithm Based on Decomposition, IEEE Transactions on Evolutionary Computation 11(6), 712-731
algorithms.implementation: Tchebycheff decomposition into neighboring scalar subproblems with differential reproduction and ideal-point updates.
algorithms.assumptions: Finite bounded continuous decision box, at least two finite objectives, and one explicit OptimizationSense per objective.
algorithms.convergence: No universal finite-time convergence guarantee is asserted; the implementation preserves the named multiobjective mechanism.

algorithms.name: Multiobjective Particle Swarm Optimizer
algorithms.time: O(ND+AM) swarm motion and repository maintenance per iteration
algorithms.applicability: Bounded continuous native multiobjective Pareto optimization
algorithms.publication: Coello Coello, Pulido & Lechuga (2004), Handling Multiple Objectives With Particle Swarm Optimization, IEEE Transactions on Evolutionary Computation 8(3), 256-279
algorithms.implementation: Pareto-repository PSO with adaptive hypercubes, inverse-density leader selection, pbest dominance and decaying mutation.
algorithms.assumptions: Finite bounded continuous decision box, at least two finite objectives, and one explicit OptimizationSense per objective.
algorithms.convergence: No universal finite-time convergence guarantee is asserted; the implementation preserves the named multiobjective mechanism.

algorithms.time: O(ND+AM) speed-constrained swarm motion and archive maintenance
algorithms.applicability: Bounded continuous native multiobjective Pareto optimization
algorithms.publication: Nebro, Durillo, Garcia-Nieto, Coello Coello, Luna & Alba (2009), SMPSO: A New PSO-Based Metaheuristic for Multi-objective Optimization, IEEE MCDM 2009, 66-73
algorithms.implementation: Speed-constrained MOPSO with constriction, componentwise velocity bounds, polynomial turbulence and external archive.
algorithms.assumptions: Finite bounded continuous decision box, at least two finite objectives, and one explicit OptimizationSense per objective.

algorithms.applicability: Bounded continuous native multiobjective Pareto optimization
algorithms.publication: Deb & Jain (2014), An Evolutionary Many-Objective Optimization Algorithm Using Reference-Point-Based Nondominated Sorting Approach, Part I, IEEE Transactions on Evolutionary Computation 18(4), 577-601
algorithms.implementation: NSGA-II framework with normalized objective vectors, Das-Dennis reference directions and reference niching.
algorithms.assumptions: Finite bounded continuous decision box, at least two finite objectives, and one explicit OptimizationSense per objective.
algorithms.convergence: No universal finite-time convergence guarantee is asserted; the implementation preserves the named multiobjective mechanism.

algorithms.applicability: Bounded continuous native multiobjective Pareto optimization
algorithms.publication: Beume, Naujoks & Emmerich (2007), SMS-EMOA: Multiobjective Selection Based on Dominated Hypervolume, European Journal of Operational Research 181(3), 1653-1669

algorithms.assumptions: Finite bounded continuous decision box, at least two finite objectives, and one explicit OptimizationSense per objective.
algorithms.convergence: No universal finite-time convergence guarantee is asserted; the implementation preserves the named multiobjective mechanism.

algorithms.applicability: Bounded continuous native multiobjective Pareto optimization
algorithms.publication: Cheng, Jin, Olhofer & Sendhoff (2016), A Reference Vector Guided Evolutionary Algorithm for Many-Objective Optimization, IEEE Transactions on Evolutionary Computation 20(5), 773-791
algorithms.implementation: Reference-vector guided many-objective selection using angle-penalized distance normalized by nearest reference-vector angle and periodic vector adaptation.
algorithms.assumptions: Finite bounded continuous decision box, at least two finite objectives, and one explicit OptimizationSense per objective.
algorithms.convergence: No universal finite-time convergence guarantee is asserted; the implementation preserves the named multiobjective mechanism.

algorithms.name: Strength Pareto Evolutionary Algorithm
algorithms.time: O(N^2M) dominance/strength work plus objective evaluations per generation
algorithms.applicability: Bounded continuous native multiobjective Pareto optimization
algorithms.publication: Zitzler & Thiele (1999), Multiobjective Evolutionary Algorithms: A Comparative Case Study and the Strength Pareto Approach, IEEE Transactions on Evolutionary Computation 3(4), 257-271
algorithms.implementation: Original SPEA with an external nondominated set, strength fitness assignment and archive clustering/truncation.
algorithms.update: \begin{aligned}S(i)&=\frac{|\{j:i\prec j\}|}{N},\\F(j)&=1+\sum_{i\in A,\ i\prec j}S(i),\qquad A^+=\operatorname{ND}(P\cup A).\end{aligned}
algorithms.assumptions: Finite bounded continuous decision box, finite objective values, at least two objectives and one explicit OptimizationSense per objective.
